object.content:
Now that there's a ton of ways to sync your files to the cloud (see http://www.theverge.com/2012/4/24/2954960/google-drive-dropbox-skydrive-sugarsync-cloud-storage-competition), I was thinking all day on how I plan to use them all. I primarily use Dropbox, Microsoft SkyDrive, and now Google Drive.

I plan on using SkyDrive to backup my photos and videos I've taken that are currently scattered over my computer, flash drives, and a backup hard drive. It's best for media like this because of it's 25 GB of storage space. On Google Drive I would like to keep all of my documents so I can edit them easily anywhere, since Drive seems to be best suited for that. And finally I'll use Dropbox for everything that's left over (current projects, things I want to easily get a hold of on my iPhone, and shared items). It's also best for cross-platform so I can sync files between Windows 7 and Ubuntu. Hopefully all of these choices will help me get my digital media more organized.
